column1: # The equivalence case matrix, TAB-separated: name<TAB>entry<TAB>args
# THE SEPARATOR IS A REAL TAB. This file was first written space-aligned for
# readability; `read -r name entry args` with IFS=tab then put the whole line
# into $name, every case ran with NO arguments, and all 29 goldens recorded the
# same default invocation -- reported as 29 passes. Nothing in the output said
# so; the case count and the file count were both plausible. If you edit this
# file, do not let an editor expand tabs.
# `entry` is `main` or `write_fastq`. --fastq and --outfolder come from the
# harness; write_fastq additionally consumes the `default` case's clustering.
# Only parameters that can change output are swept. --t is NOT a performance
# knob: on the smoke corpus --t 1 gives 40 clusters and --t 8 gives 35. It
# selects a different algorithm (hierarchical batch merge vs a single pass), so
# each --t value is its own case.
# --isoseq is exactly --k 15 --w 50 and --ont is exactly --k 13 --w 20, so the
# explicit k/w cases below cover the presets; only one preset case is kept, to
# pin that the preset still resolves to those values.
